source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Public Esther 7–10 binds the 62 matching original Hebrew records, including all source notes. The earlier 105 records remain bound in the Esther 1–6 ledger.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Reconnect the interrupted journey to the banquet without supplying an unstated motive.
verses.before: So the king and Haman came to drink with Queen Esther.
verses.after: So the king and Haman came to drink with Queen Esther.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the king and Haman came to drink with Queen Esther.

verses.rationale: Repeat the paired petition and request and the extravagant royal offer from chapter 5.
verses.before: On the second day, while they were drinking wine at the feast, the king said again to Esther, “What is your petition, Queen Esther? It will be given to you. And what is your request? Even to half the kingdom, it will be done.”
verses.after: On this second day, as they drank wine, the king again asked Esther, “What is your petition, Queen Esther? It will be granted. What is your request? Even if it is half the kingdom, it will be done.”
verses.tsw_comparator: On the second day, while they were drinking wine at the feast, the king said again to Esther, “What is your petition, Queen Esther? It shall be given to you. And what is your request? Even to half the kingdom, it shall be done.”

verses.rationale: Make the life-and-people parallel audible and retain its connection to the king’s repeated questions.
verses.before: Then Queen Esther answered and said, “If I have found favor in your eyes, O king, and if it is good to the king, let my life be given to me at my petition, and my people at my request.
verses.after: Queen Esther answered, “If I have won your favor, Your Majesty, and if it pleases the king, grant me my life—that is my petition—and the lives of my people—that is my request.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Queen Esther answered and said, “If I have found favor in your eyes, O king, and if it is good to the king, let my life be given to me at my petition, and my people at my request.

verses.rationale: Retain the threefold destruction formula and enslaved men and women; mark the difficult final clause’s alternative reading in a note.
verses.before: For we have been sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, killed, and annihilated. If we had merely been sold as male and female servants, I would have remained silent, for the distress would not have been worth troubling the king.”
verses.after: For my people and I have been sold to be destroyed, killed, and annihilated. If we had only been sold as male and female slaves, I would have kept silent, for such distress would not justify troubling the king.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For we have been sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, killed, and annihilated. If we had merely been sold as male and female servants, I would have remained silent, for the distress would not have been worth troubling the king.”

verses.rationale: Render the filled-heart idiom as daring and retain the two urgent questions.
verses.before: Then King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther, “Who is he, and where is he, whose heart has filled him to do this?”
verses.after: King Ahasuerus demanded of Queen Esther, “Who is he? Where is the man who has dared to do this?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther, “Who is he, and where is he, whose heart has filled him to do this?”

verses.rationale: Keep the paired accusation and abrupt identification in Esther’s voice.
verses.before: Esther said, “An adversary and enemy—this wicked Haman!” Then Haman was terrified before the king and queen.
verses.after: Esther said, “An adversary and an enemy—this wicked Haman!” Haman was terrified before the king and queen.
verses.tsw_comparator: Esther said, “An adversary and enemy—this wicked Haman!” Then Haman was terrified before the king and queen.

verses.rationale: Distinguish the king’s departure from Haman’s remaining plea without inventing an escape attempt.
verses.before: The king arose in his fury from the wine feast and went into the palace garden, but Haman remained to seek his life from Queen Esther, for he saw that disaster had been determined against him by the king.
verses.after: The king rose in fury from the wine banquet and went into the palace garden. Haman stayed behind to plead with Queen Esther for his life, for he saw that the king had determined his destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king arose in his fury from the wine feast and went into the palace garden, but Haman remained to seek his life from Queen Esther, for he saw that disaster had been determined against him by the king.

verses.rationale: Keep the king’s accusation distinct from the narrator’s description; preserve the face covering and ambiguous falling posture.
verses.before: When the king returned from the palace garden to the house of the wine feast, Haman had fallen upon the couch where Esther was. Then the king said, “Will he even assault the queen with me in the house?” As the word went out from the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.
verses.after: When the king returned from the palace garden to the banquet hall, Haman was falling onto the couch where Esther lay. The king exclaimed, “Will he even assault the queen while I am here in the house?” As soon as the words left the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the king returned from the palace garden to the house of the wine feast, Haman had fallen upon the couch where Esther was. Then the king said, “Will he even assault the queen with me in the house?” As the word went out from the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.

verses.rationale: Retain the witness’s appeal to Mordecai’s service, the height, and the reversal of the intended victim.
verses.before: Then Harbona, one of the eunuchs before the king, said, “Look, the tree that Haman made for Mordecai, who spoke good for the king, is standing at Haman’s house, fifty cubits high.” The king said, “Hang him on it.”
verses.after: Then Harbona, one of the eunuchs attending the king, said, “There is also the stake Haman made for Mordecai, who spoke to save the king. It stands at Haman’s house, fifty cubits high.” The king said, “Hang him on it!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Harbona, one of the eunuchs before the king, said, “Look, the tree that Haman made for Mordecai, who spoke good for the king, is standing at Haman’s house, fifty cubits high.” The king said, “Hang him on it.”

verses.rationale: Repeat the prepared-for-Mordecai detail and close with the king’s changed anger, not a claim that all danger has ended.
verses.before: So they hanged Haman on the tree that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then the king’s fury subsided.
verses.after: They hung Haman on the stake he had prepared for Mordecai. Then the king’s fury subsided.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they hanged Haman on the tree that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then the king’s fury subsided.

verses.rationale: Render house as estate in the transfer while retaining the relationship that gives Mordecai access.
verses.before: On that day King Ahasuerus gave Queen Esther the house of Haman, enemy of the Judeans. Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had told what he was to her.
verses.after: That day King Ahasuerus gave Queen Esther the estate of Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Mordecai came into the king’s presence, because Esther had explained how he was related to her.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day King Ahasuerus gave Queen Esther the house of Haman, enemy of the Judeans. Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had told what he was to her.

verses.rationale: Keep the two distinct transfers: royal authority and management of the estate.
verses.before: The king removed his signet ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. Esther appointed Mordecai over the house of Haman.
verses.after: The king removed his signet ring, which he had taken back from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman’s estate.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king removed his signet ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. Esther appointed Mordecai over the house of Haman.

verses.rationale: Preserve her repeated intervention and bodily grief after Haman’s death.
verses.before: Esther spoke again before the king. She fell before his feet, wept, and sought his favor to turn away the evil of Haman the Agagite and the plan that he had devised against the Judeans.
verses.after: Esther spoke to the king again. She fell at his feet, wept, and begged him to undo the evil of Haman the Agagite and the scheme he had devised against the Jews.
verses.tsw_comparator: Esther spoke again before the king. She fell before his feet, wept, and sought his favor to turn away the evil of Haman the Agagite and the plan that he had devised against the Judeans.

verses.rationale: Retain the scepter gesture and her movement from the floor to standing.
verses.before: The king extended the gold scepter to Esther, and Esther arose and stood before the king.
verses.after: The king extended the gold scepter to Esther, and she rose and stood before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king extended the gold scepter to Esther, and Esther arose and stood before the king.

verses.rationale: Keep the accumulating conditions and request to reverse the existing written decree.
verses.before: She said, “If it is good to the king, and if I have found favor before him, and if the matter is right before the king, and I am good in his eyes, let it be written to revoke the letters devised by Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Judeans who are in all the king’s provinces.
verses.after: She said, “If it pleases the king, if I have won his favor, if he considers it right, and if he is pleased with me, let an order be written to revoke the letters devised by Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews in every royal province.
verses.tsw_comparator: She said, “If it is good to the king, and if I have found favor before him, and if the matter is right before the king, and I am good in his eyes, let it be written to revoke the letters devised by Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Judeans who are in all the king’s provinces.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated personal question and the distinct people and kinship terms.
verses.before: For how can I bear to see the evil that will come upon my people? And how can I bear to see the destruction of my kindred?”
verses.after: How could I bear to see the disaster that would overtake my people? How could I bear to see my own family destroyed?”
verses.tsw_comparator: For how can I bear to see the evil that will come upon my people? And how can I bear to see the destruction of my kindred?”

verses.rationale: Keep the king’s recital of what he has done without implying it has solved the decree’s consequences.
verses.before: Then King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther and Mordecai the Judean, “Look, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and they have hanged him on the tree because he stretched out his hand against the Judeans.
verses.after: King Ahasuerus told Queen Esther and Mordecai the Jew, “I have given Haman’s estate to Esther, and they have hung him on the stake because he raised his hand against the Jews.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther and Mordecai the Judean, “Look, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and they have hanged him on the tree because he stretched out his hand against the Judeans.

verses.rationale: Preserve delegated discretion and the stated obstacle to rescinding the first decree.
verses.before: Now you yourselves write concerning the Judeans as is good in your eyes, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s signet ring. For a document written in the king’s name and sealed with the king’s signet ring cannot be revoked.”
verses.after: Now you may write concerning the Jews as you see fit, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s signet ring. A document written in the king’s name and sealed with his ring cannot be revoked.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now you yourselves write concerning the Judeans as is good in your eyes, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s signet ring. For a document written in the king’s name and sealed with the king’s signet ring cannot be revoked.”

verses.rationale: Retain the complete date, administrative groups, territory and count, and explicit addition of the Jews’ script and language.
verses.before: Then the king’s scribes were called at that time, in the third month, which is the month of Sivan, on the twenty-third day. It was written according to all that Mordecai commanded concerning the Judeans, to the satraps, governors, and officials of the provinces from India to Cush, one hundred twenty-seven provinces, to each province in its script and to each people in its language, and to the Judeans in their own script and their own language.
verses.after: The king’s scribes were summoned at once, on the twenty-third day of the third month, the month of Sivan. Everything Mordecai commanded was written to the Jews, the satraps, the governors, and the officials of the 127 provinces from India to Cush—to each province in its own script and each people in its own language, and to the Jews in their own script and language.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king’s scribes were called at that time, in the third month, which is the month of Sivan, on the twenty-third day. It was written according to all that Mordecai commanded concerning the Judeans, to the satraps, governors, and officials of the provinces from India to Cush, one hundred twenty-seven provinces, to each province in its script and to each people in its language, and to the Judeans in their own script and their own language.

verses.rationale: Render the difficult horse terminology as royal-bred swift mounts, with uncertainty noted rather than inventing distinct species.
verses.before: He wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus, sealed it with the king’s signet ring, and sent letters by the hand of mounted couriers riding on swift royal horses bred from the royal stud.
verses.after: He wrote in King Ahasuerus’s name, sealed the letters with the king’s signet ring, and sent them by mounted couriers riding swift horses bred from the royal herd.
verses.tsw_comparator: He wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus, sealed it with the king’s signet ring, and sent letters by the hand of mounted couriers riding on swift royal horses bred from the royal stud.

verses.rationale: Keep the defensive authorization and the decree’s harmful breadth, including children and women; note the alternative grammatical attachment.
verses.before: In them the king granted the Judeans who were in every city permission to gather together and stand for their lives, to destroy, kill, and annihilate every armed force of any people or province that attacked them, including children and women, and to plunder their possessions,
verses.after: The king permitted the Jews in every city to gather and defend their lives: to destroy, kill, and annihilate any armed force of a people or province that attacked them, including children and women, and to plunder their property,
verses.tsw_comparator: In them the king granted the Judeans who were in every city permission to gather together and stand for their lives, to destroy, kill, and annihilate every armed force of any people or province that attacked them, including children and women, and to plunder their possessions,

verses.rationale: Continue the authorization across the label and preserve the date matching the original decree.
verses.before: on one day throughout all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar.
verses.after: on a single day throughout King Ahasuerus’s provinces—the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar.
verses.tsw_comparator: on one day throughout all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar.

verses.rationale: Retain revenge explicitly rather than reducing the clause to protection alone.
verses.before: A copy of the document was to be issued as law in every province, publicly displayed to all peoples, so that the Judeans would be ready on that day to take vengeance on their enemies.
verses.after: A copy of the document was to be issued as law in every province and made known to all the peoples, so that the Jews would be ready on that day to take revenge on their enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: A copy of the document was to be issued as law in every province, publicly displayed to all peoples, so that the Judeans would be ready on that day to take vengeance on their enemies.

verses.rationale: Repeat the urgency and distinguish imperial delivery from publication at the court.
verses.before: The couriers mounted on the swift royal horses went out hurried and pressed by the king’s command, and the law was issued in the citadel of Susa.
verses.after: The couriers rode out on the swift royal horses, hurried along by the king’s command. The decree was also issued in the citadel of Susa.
verses.tsw_comparator: The couriers mounted on the swift royal horses went out hurried and pressed by the king’s command, and the law was issued in the citadel of Susa.

verses.rationale: Retain the colors, crown, and fabric display, contrasting the city’s earlier bewilderment with joy.
verses.before: Mordecai went out from before the king in royal garments of blue and white, with a great crown of gold and a robe of fine linen and purple. And the city of Susa shouted and rejoiced.
verses.after: Mordecai left the king’s presence wearing royal clothing of blue-violet and white, a great gold crown, and a mantle of fine linen and purple wool. The city of Susa shouted for joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Mordecai went out from before the king in royal garments of blue and white, with a great crown of gold and a robe of fine linen and purple. And the city of Susa shouted and rejoiced.

verses.rationale: Keep light as an image and the four-part celebratory cadence.
verses.before: For the Judeans there was light and gladness, joy and honor.
verses.after: For the Jews there was light and joy, gladness and honor.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the Judeans there was light and gladness, joy and honor.

verses.rationale: Render the rare verb without asserting the exact form of conversion; retain fear as the stated motive.
verses.before: In every province and in every city, wherever the king’s command and his law reached, there was gladness and joy among the Judeans, a feast and a good day. And many from the peoples of the land became Judeans, for fear of the Judeans had fallen upon them.
verses.after: In every province and every city reached by the king’s command and decree, the Jews celebrated with joy and gladness, banquets and a holiday. Many among the peoples of the land declared themselves Jews, because fear of the Jews had fallen on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: In every province and in every city, wherever the king’s command and his law reached, there was gladness and joy among the Judeans, a feast and a good day. And many from the peoples of the land became Judeans, for fear of the Judeans had fallen upon them.

verses.rationale: Make the explicit reversal the sentence’s pivot while keeping the precise date and opposing groups.
verses.before: In the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar, on its thirteenth day, when the king’s command and law were to be carried out, on the day when the enemies of the Judeans hoped to rule over them, the opposite happened: the Judeans themselves ruled over people who hated them.
verses.after: On the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, the king’s command and decree were due to take effect. The Jews’ enemies had hoped to overpower them that day, but the reverse happened: the Jews overpowered those who hated them.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar, on its thirteenth day, when the king’s command and law were to be carried out, on the day when the enemies of the Judeans hoped to rule over them, the opposite happened: the Judeans themselves ruled over those who hated them.

verses.rationale: Retain the objects of the attack and the narrator’s explanation of their opponents’ inability to stand.
verses.before: The Judeans gathered in their cities throughout all the provinces of King Ahasuerus to lay hands on people who sought their harm. No one stood before them, for fear of them had fallen upon all the peoples.
verses.after: The Jews gathered in their cities throughout King Ahasuerus’s provinces to strike those who sought their harm. No one could withstand them, for fear of them had fallen on all the peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Judeans gathered in their cities throughout all the provinces of King Ahasuerus to lay hands on those who sought their harm. No one stood before them, for fear of them had fallen upon all the peoples.

verses.rationale: Keep all four administrative groups and their stated motive rather than attributing benevolence.
verses.before: All the officials of the provinces, the satraps, the governors, and those doing the king’s business supported the Judeans, for fear of Mordecai had fallen upon them.
verses.after: All the provincial officials, satraps, governors, and those who conducted the king’s business supported the Jews, because fear of Mordecai had fallen on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the officials of the provinces, the satraps, the governors, and those doing the king’s business supported the Judeans, for fear of Mordecai had fallen upon them.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated growth in power and the emphatic renewed naming.
verses.before: For Mordecai was great in the king’s house, and his fame went out throughout all the provinces, for the man Mordecai grew greater and greater.
verses.after: Mordecai was powerful in the king’s palace, and his reputation spread through all the provinces. The man Mordecai was growing more and more powerful.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Mordecai was great in the king’s house, and his fame went out throughout all the provinces, for the man Mordecai grew greater and greater.

verses.rationale: Retain the violence and discretionary action without inserting a limiting defense formula not present in this verse.
verses.before: The Judeans struck all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, killing and destroying, and did as they pleased to people who hated them.
verses.after: The Jews struck all their enemies with the sword, killing and destroying them. They did as they pleased to those who hated them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Judeans struck all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, killing and destroying, and did as they pleased to those who hated them.

verses.rationale: Keep both verbs and the exact local casualty count.
verses.before: In the citadel of Susa the Judeans killed and destroyed five hundred men.
verses.after: In the citadel of Susa, the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the citadel of Susa the Judeans killed and destroyed five hundred men.

verses.rationale: Start the ten-name list as a continuation of the killing account.
verses.before: They also killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,
verses.after: They also killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,
verses.tsw_comparator: They also killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,

verses.rationale: Retain the second three names in their source order.
verses.before: Poratha, Adalia, Parmashta,
verses.after: Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,
verses.tsw_comparator: Poratha, Adalia, Parmashta,

verses.rationale: Retain the four concluding names, keeping Arisai and Aridai distinct.
verses.before: Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha,
verses.after: Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha—
verses.tsw_comparator: Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha,

verses.rationale: Complete the list’s identification and preserve the first of three explicit refusals to plunder.
verses.before: the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, enemy of the Judeans. But they did not lay their hands on the plunder.
verses.after: the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews. But they did not lay hands on the plunder.
verses.tsw_comparator: the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, enemy of the Judeans. But they did not lay their hands on the plunder.

verses.rationale: Keep the report distinct from the events already narrated.
verses.before: On that day the number of those killed in the citadel of Susa came before the king.
verses.after: That day the number killed in the citadel of Susa was reported to the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day the number of those killed in the citadel of Susa came before the king.

verses.rationale: Retain the reported counts, rhetorical question, and renewed petition/request formula.
verses.before: The king said to Queen Esther, “In the citadel of Susa the Judeans have killed and destroyed five hundred men and the ten sons of Haman. What then have they done in the rest of the king’s provinces? Now what is your petition? It will be given to you. What is your further request? It will be done.”
verses.after: The king said to Queen Esther, “In the citadel of Susa, the Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men and Haman’s ten sons. What must they have done in the other royal provinces! Now what is your petition? It will be granted. What further request do you have? It will be done.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king said to Queen Esther, “In the citadel of Susa the Judeans have killed and destroyed five hundred men and the ten sons of Haman. What then have they done in the rest of the king’s provinces? Now what is your petition? It shall be given to you. What is your further request? It shall be done.”

verses.rationale: Preserve Esther’s request for another day and postmortem display; do not soften or justify it.
verses.before: Esther said, “If it is good to the king, let the Judeans who are in Susa be permitted tomorrow also to act according to today’s law, and let the ten sons of Haman be hanged on the tree.”
verses.after: Esther answered, “If it pleases the king, let the Jews in Susa act tomorrow as today’s decree permits. And let Haman’s ten sons be hung on the stake.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Esther said, “If it is good to the king, let the Judeans who are in Susa be permitted tomorrow also to act according to today’s law, and let the ten sons of Haman be hanged on the tree.”

verses.rationale: Keep implementation and the sons’ hanging distinct from their earlier death.
verses.before: The king commanded it to be done. A law was issued in Susa, and they hanged the ten sons of Haman.
verses.after: The king ordered this done. A decree was issued in Susa, and Haman’s ten sons were hung.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king commanded it to be done. A law was issued in Susa, and they hanged the ten sons of Haman.

verses.rationale: Retain the second day’s date and count and repeat the no-plunder refrain.
verses.before: The Judeans who were in Susa gathered also on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar and killed three hundred men in Susa, but they did not lay their hands on the plunder.
verses.after: The Jews in Susa gathered again on the fourteenth day of Adar and killed three hundred men in Susa. But they did not lay hands on the plunder.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Judeans who were in Susa gathered also on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar and killed three hundred men in Susa, but they did not lay their hands on the plunder.

verses.rationale: Keep the defensive framing, large stated death toll, and third no-plunder refrain without harmonizing the figure.
verses.before: The rest of the Judeans who were in the king’s provinces gathered and stood for their lives and gained rest from their enemies. They killed seventy-five thousand of people who hated them, but they did not lay their hands on the plunder.
verses.after: The other Jews in the king’s provinces gathered to defend their lives and gain relief from their enemies. They killed seventy-five thousand of those who hated them. But they did not lay hands on the plunder.
verses.tsw_comparator: The rest of the Judeans who were in the king’s provinces gathered and stood for their lives and gained rest from their enemies. They killed seventy-five thousand of those who hated them, but they did not lay their hands on the plunder.

verses.rationale: Clarify which day involved fighting and which involved rest while preserving the dated sequence.
verses.before: This was on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, and on the fourteenth day they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
verses.after: This happened on the thirteenth day of Adar. On the fourteenth they rested and made it a day of banqueting and joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: This was on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, and on the fourteenth day they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

verses.rationale: Retain the contrast that explains Susa’s different celebration date.
verses.before: But the Judeans who were in Susa gathered on the thirteenth and on the fourteenth, and on the fifteenth they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
verses.after: The Jews in Susa, however, gathered on both the thirteenth and fourteenth. They rested on the fifteenth and made it a day of banqueting and joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the Judeans who were in Susa gathered on the thirteenth and on the fourteenth, and on the fifteenth they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

verses.rationale: Follow the reading tradition for rural Jews and preserve reciprocal gifts alongside feasting.
verses.before: So the rural Judeans who live in the unwalled towns make the fourteenth day of the month of Adar a day of gladness and feasting, a good day, and a day of sending portions to one another.
verses.after: That is why Jews in the countryside, those living in unwalled towns, celebrate the fourteenth day of Adar with joy, banqueting, and a holiday, sending portions of food to one another.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore the rural Judeans who live in the unwalled towns make the fourteenth day of the month of Adar a day of gladness and feasting, a good day, and a day of sending portions to one another.

verses.rationale: Keep the written record and geographical reach while continuing the purpose into the next verse.
verses.before: Mordecai wrote these things and sent letters to all the Judeans who were in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, near and far,
verses.after: Mordecai recorded these events and sent letters to all the Jews in every province of King Ahasuerus, near and far,
verses.tsw_comparator: Mordecai wrote these things and sent letters to all the Judeans who were in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, near and far,

verses.rationale: Preserve both dates and the annual obligation without collapsing the local distinctions.
verses.before: establishing for them that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month of Adar and the fifteenth day of it, year by year,
verses.after: requiring them to observe the fourteenth and fifteenth days of Adar every year,
verses.tsw_comparator: establishing for them that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month of Adar and the fifteenth day of it, year by year,

verses.rationale: Keep the paired reversals and distinguish reciprocal food gifts from aid to poor people.
verses.before: as the days on which the Judeans gained rest from their enemies, and the month that was turned for them from sorrow to gladness and from mourning to a good day, so that they should make them days of feasting and gladness, sending portions to one another and gifts to the poor.
verses.after: as the days when the Jews gained relief from their enemies, and the month when sorrow turned to joy and mourning to a holiday. They were to make these days a time of banqueting and joy, sending food to one another and gifts to the poor.
verses.tsw_comparator: as the days on which the Judeans gained rest from their enemies, and the month that was turned for them from sorrow to gladness and from mourning to a good day, so that they should make them days of feasting and gladness, sending portions to one another and gifts to the poor.

verses.rationale: Retain both existing practice and written instruction as the grounds of acceptance.
verses.before: So the Judeans accepted what they had begun to do and what Mordecai had written to them.
verses.after: The Jews accepted what they had already begun to practice and what Mordecai had written to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the Judeans accepted what they had begun to do and what Mordecai had written to them.

verses.rationale: Repeat the full enemy identification and lot explanation, preserving the intended panic as well as destruction.
verses.before: For Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, enemy of all the Judeans, had plotted against the Judeans to destroy them and had cast Pur—that is, the lot—to crush and destroy them.
verses.after: For Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted to destroy them. He had cast the Pur—that is, the lot—to throw them into panic and destroy them.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, enemy of all the Judeans, had plotted against the Judeans to destroy them and had cast Pur—that is, the lot—to crush and destroy them.

verses.rationale: Render the ambiguous feminine coming-clause as the matter’s arrival, with Esther as an alternative in the note; keep the summary’s compressed chronology.
verses.before: But when it came before the king, he commanded by letter that Haman’s evil plan that he had devised against the Judeans should return upon his own head and that he and his sons should be hanged on the tree.
verses.after: But when the matter came before the king, he ordered in writing that Haman’s evil scheme against the Jews should come back on his own head. Haman and his sons were hung on the stake.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when it came before the king, he commanded by letter that Haman’s evil plan that he had devised against the Judeans should return upon his own head and that he and his sons should be hanged on the tree.

verses.rationale: Retain the name explanation and the sentence’s accumulating grounds before its continuation.
verses.before: So they called these days Purim, after the name Pur. Therefore, because of all the words of this letter, and what they had seen concerning this, and what had come upon them,
verses.after: That is why these days were called Purim, after the word Pur. Because of everything in this letter, and because of what they had seen and what had happened to them,
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore they called these days Purim, after the name Pur. Therefore, because of all the words of this letter, and what they had seen concerning this, and what had come upon them,

verses.rationale: Follow the plural reading tradition and preserve the obligation’s extension to descendants and new adherents.
verses.before: the Judeans established and accepted for themselves, for their offspring, and for everyone who joined them, so that it should not pass away, that they would keep these two days according to what was written and according to their appointed time every year.
verses.after: the Jews established and accepted an enduring obligation for themselves, their descendants, and all who joined them: to observe these two days every year, as written and at the appointed time.
verses.tsw_comparator: the Judeans established and accepted for themselves, for their offspring, and for all who joined them, so that it should not pass away, that they would keep these two days according to what was written and according to their appointed time every year.

verses.rationale: Preserve the fourfold distributive repetition and the paired commitment to observance and memory.
verses.before: These days are to be remembered and kept in every generation, every clan, every province, and every city. These days of Purim will not pass away from among the Judeans, and their remembrance will not cease from their offspring.
verses.after: These days were to be remembered and observed in every generation, every family, every province, and every city. These days of Purim must never cease among the Jews, nor their memory disappear from their descendants.
verses.tsw_comparator: These days are to be remembered and kept in every generation, every clan, every province, and every city. These days of Purim shall not pass away from among the Judeans, and their remembrance shall not cease from their offspring.

verses.rationale: Keep Esther’s named parentage and leading role, with Mordecai’s participation and the second-letter designation.
verses.before: Then Queen Esther daughter of Abihail and Mordecai the Judean wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter concerning Purim.
verses.after: Queen Esther daughter of Abihail, together with Mordecai the Jew, wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter concerning Purim.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Queen Esther daughter of Abihail and Mordecai the Judean wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter concerning Purim.

verses.rationale: Retain the switch to a masculine singular sender and the province count; render truth as reliable assurance in this letter’s greeting.
verses.before: Letters were sent to all the Judeans, to the one hundred twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, words of peace and faithfulness,
verses.after: He sent letters to all the Jews in the 127 provinces of Ahasuerus’s kingdom, with words of peace and assurance,
verses.tsw_comparator: Letters were sent to all the Judeans, to the one hundred twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, words of peace and faithfulness,

verses.rationale: Keep both authorities and the reference to fasting and cries without importing a later festival calendar.
verses.before: to establish these days of Purim at their appointed times, just as Mordecai the Judean and Queen Esther had established for them, and just as they had established for themselves and for their offspring matters of fasting and their cry.
verses.after: confirming the days of Purim at their appointed times, as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had established for them, and as they had established for themselves and their descendants the practices of fasting and lamenting.
verses.tsw_comparator: to establish these days of Purim at their appointed times, just as Mordecai the Judean and Queen Esther had established for them, and just as they had established for themselves and for their offspring matters of fasting and their cry.

verses.rationale: Retain Esther’s final authorizing word and the written record without identifying an unstated book.
verses.before: Esther’s command established these matters of Purim, and it was written in the book.
verses.after: Esther’s decree confirmed these matters concerning Purim, and it was recorded in a book.
verses.tsw_comparator: Esther’s command established these matters of Purim, and it was written in the book.

verses.rationale: Keep the final imperial levy and maritime extent rather than turning the ending into unqualified liberation.
verses.before: King Ahasuerus imposed tribute upon the land and the coastlands of the sea.
verses.after: King Ahasuerus imposed tribute on the mainland and the islands of the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: King Ahasuerus imposed tribute upon the land and the coastlands of the sea.

verses.rationale: Preserve the archival question and the reversed Media/Persia order found here.
verses.before: And all the acts of his power and his might, and the full account of the greatness of Mordecai to which the king raised him—are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?
verses.after: All his acts of power and might, and the full account of Mordecai’s greatness to which the king raised him—are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Media and Persia?
verses.tsw_comparator: And all the acts of his power and his might, and the full account of the greatness of Mordecai to which the king raised him—are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?

verses.rationale: Retain second rank and the qualified many rather than unanimous approval; render the final seed reference corporately, with the literal wording noted.
verses.before: For Mordecai the Judean was second to King Ahasuerus, great among the Judeans and pleasing to the multitude of his brothers, seeking the good of his people and speaking peace to all his offspring.
verses.after: Mordecai the Jew ranked second to King Ahasuerus. He was great among the Jews and esteemed by the many among his brothers, seeking his people’s good and speaking for the well-being of all his people.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Mordecai the Judean was second to King Ahasuerus, great among the Judeans and pleasing to the multitude of his brothers, seeking the good of his people and speaking peace to all his offspring.
